entries.title: Widget looks to pick: the flat battery ring, clock and card are replaced by depth candidates
entries.lede: The first widget parts were rejected as flat, so this is a design pass with references first (design/23-WIDGETS.md: the reference desktop's widget style, phone widget conventions, Windows 11 widgets, and Fantastical, Notion Calendar, Amie, Google Calendar and Vimcal for the calendar brief) and rendered candidates second, at 2x over a calm wallpaper. Every candidate keeps the same props, so the shell's wiring does not change; only the look does. The rule now recorded: nothing flat, every part carries a material cue (an inset well, a raised boss, a bezel, a gloss, the plate bevel the app icons use) and a type-hierarchy cue (the display face for the hero number, the data face for labels). The calendar widget is not restyled here: it is queued to the downstream widgets pass, alongside the plan for a calendar app that connects to cloud providers.
notes: Picks needed (design/23 §6): battery gauge Well, Cell, or both (proposed: Cell for the Small widget, Well for the Medium's row of devices); clock dial Bezel or Sky (proposed: Sky for the Medium's four dials, Bezel for the Large); should the Lit card finish become the default for desktop widgets (proposed: yes); hero number 34 or 40 px; day/night by sunrise and sunset where the zone is known (proposed) or fixed 06:00–18:00; calendar month load as dots (proposed) or a heat tint; the Small calendar as a date face with the next event (proposed) or the compact month grid; numerals on the dial none (proposed) or 12/3/6/9; the Small clock's day/night cue as the 16 px sky disc or a 40 px dial in the corner.

What each candidate does: Well puts the ring in a groove pressed into the plate around a raised disc that holds the device glyph, the level as a glossy arc and the charging bolt as a lit disc; Cell is a recessed capsule bed holding a glossy liquid as wide as the level with a terminal cap, low and critical recolouring only the liquid; Bezel is a raised rim round a recessed sky face with a minute track, tapered hands over a shadow and an accent-ringed hub; Sky sinks the whole dial into the plate with the sky as its ground; Lit adds the icon plate's bevel, a sheen down the top and a shaded foot to the card. Day dials are always the pale pair and night dials the slate pair, whatever the desktop's scheme.

Known weak spot: in the light scheme the Lit finish reads through tonal falloff and the deeper drop rather than a visible top line, because the card is near white. Sheets are 2x only; fractional scales unchecked.

entries.title: The shell's Milestone 10 gets its calendar, widgets, screenshot thumbnail and hot corners; sill's adoption is next
entries.lede: quire cut the design parts for the shell's Milestone 10 today, on quire master and shell-host master together. MonthGrid (design/04 §39) lays a month across seven columns with weekday initials, quiets the neighbouring month's days, seats today on the accent disc, marks busy days with a dot, offers an optional ISO week column, and slides the whole grid in from whichever side the new month came from on previous/next. WidgetFrame (design/04 §40) comes in small, medium and large on a 164 px cell with a 16 px gap: a card on the Widget material over the desktop, or a flat tile inside the notification center, sized by WidgetMetrics and pulsing once when its value bumps; inside sit ClockFace, analog with separate day and night faces and an accent second hand, or digital, and LevelRing for the battery with low and critical tones and a charging bolt. ShotThumbnail (design/04 §41) is the floating screenshot card, 240 px wide and letterboxed between 2:1 and 16:10 (pillarboxed for a portrait shot), rising in with a spring and sliding out on dismiss, with hover actions, swipe-to-dismiss riding the same swipe machine as a notification, a drag threshold that hands off to the host, a drag ghost, and reduced motion handled inside the component. On the shell-host side, a drag source (SurfaceHandle::start_drag, F60) is now proven by dropping a file onto a terminal on the virtual compositor; F61 found that a keyboard-less surface cannot portably learn whether a modifier key is held, so the shell retires the modifier-key variant of its hot corners and keeps dwell and screen-edge triggers only. Hot corners themselves follow design/13 §13.3.12 (a 150 ms dwell, a 500 ms re-arm, and an action table), and the whole set follows design/22 §3.19-§3.23 for session, widgets, calendar, screenshot and hot_corners. quire's parts are proven; sill still has to adopt them.
notes: Earlier in the day, F59 found the host never re-dispatched pointer enter/leave after a layout-driven hover change, so a banner arriving under a resting pointer stayed unhovered; the shell's real-input repro confirmed the fix, quire's own Harness got the same repair, and BannerStack learned an entry edge.

F60 and F61 together settle the drag story: F60 proves the host can originate a drag (a file dropped onto a terminal on the virtual compositor); F61 closes off the modifier-held hot corner, since a surface with no keyboard cannot portably read a held modifier key.

Design references: design/04 §39 (MonthGrid), §40 (WidgetFrame, WidgetMetrics, ClockFace, LevelRing), §41 (ShotThumbnail); design/13 §13.3.12 (hot corners: dwell, re-arm, action table); design/22 §3.19-§3.23 (session, widgets, calendar, screenshot, hot_corners).

entries.title: The shell's Milestone 6 lands on new notification parts: card, banner stack, swipe, center panel, rich runs
entries.lede: The shell's notification server, banners and center are complete and proven with real input on the headless compositor recipe. quire supplied the parts: a notification card in the Toast material with the app mark, age, summary and a body clamped to two lines that opens to six on hover, a count chip with offset layers for groups, action buttons and an 18 px close at the top left as on macOS; a banner stack that slides cards in from the right and out again with the rows below healing; a swipe machine that follows a drag one-to-one to the right and damped to the left, springs back under a threshold and flies out past it, with horizontal scroll summed into the same offset; a right-edge full-height panel for the center; rich body runs with italics, underlines and links; and a group header. Real input then found two host pointer bugs (no hover until a second motion after entering a surface; a surface unmapped under the pointer leaving the next one without its enter), which are being fixed in shell-host.
notes: Blitz limits recorded: no line-clamp (the clamp is a max-height in whole lines with a fade drawn only where text is cut); hidden clamped lines still take hits (fixed with pointer-events); wheel deltas keep winit's sign and have no phase; removing an animation freezes its last frame; absolute boxes place against their parent.
The motion table is at 64 animations and 55 keyframes; 907 tests.

entries.title: Blitz pages become vector PDFs through pdfrum: mailo's last webview blocker falls
entries.lede: The user decided mailo goes native-only, printing included, and that the PDF must go through their own pdfrum library rather than a third-party writer. Blitz lays the page out once at the paper's content width; a painter over pdfrum's canvas draws each page as vector graphics with embedded, subsetted fonts and the real text behind every glyph run (read from the layout's clusters, so ligatures and CJK extract exactly); page breaks follow two markers since Blitz cannot parse the CSS ones, keep-together boxes move whole, orphans and widows are held, and no glyph is left hidden under a clip. Variable fonts embed at the weight the layout used. A print dialog goes through the desktop portal behind a feature. pdfrum itself gained a glyph-run API with ToUnicode and ActualText, gradient shadings, blend modes, PNG pass-through, blank documents and variable-font instancing, under its own gates.
notes: The three-page fixture (Latin, CJK, a JPEG, an alpha PNG, a moved block, a forced break): 42 KB, about 6 ms per print after the first in release, JPEG embedded byte-identical, and a rasterised page differs from the headless snapshot by a mean of half a channel level.

Two findings on the way: the prototype's thin grey CJK was the variable font's Thin default instance, not a fallback; and a glyph with no text used to swallow the next glyph's text, a bug the earlier writer had too.
pdfrum is pinned by git revision until the user publishes 0.4.0 (the whole chain together, because of a dependency pin); then quire v0.1.10 is tagged and mailo deletes its webview path.

entries.title: v0.1.9: the control center's parts, the power menu's sheet, a window frame, and the composer's surface hardened
entries.lede: One tag closes the day's second half. For the shell's Milestone 5: module tiles, a module grid and a content panel, settings rows, a pane switcher, a control-center glyph, and a compact appearance picker; for its power menu: a sheet that exits, centres and dims behind a modal scrim, buttons that can be disabled or regular-sized in the danger colour, an overlay root that fills the viewport, and keyboard-cap arrows that finally draw (the bundled mono font had dropped the left and right arrows). For our own windows: a titlebar you can drag, double-click to zoom, traffic lights with a Fill-only tiling menu, over one seam that ds-native implements for winit and the shell implements over the host. For mailo: fields focusable by handle or selector, keep-focus on clicks, frame tags and link text with hover, the editing surface's programmatic focus, pointer capture and caret width, and a tree row with drop state. And every timing test now polls for its state instead of asserting at an instant, because the harness advances real time.
notes: 823 tests; the day went from v0.1.2 to v0.1.9. All work landed through the gate worktree; the weekly usage limit stopped six agents mid-gate once and every branch resumed from its own transcript with nothing lost.

Blitz findings recorded on the way: a Dioxus-written `open` attribute never opens a details element (namespace mismatch); padding and borders are not painted on inline elements; stacking order follows CSS 2.1 Appendix E; about sixty tinted cards in one document lose layers; no pointer capture, worked around at the host.

Compositor findings for the fork list: cosmic-comp configures every floating window as tiled on all edges, and neither cosmic-comp nor KWin lets a client place its own window, so tiling from the window menu ships Fill only.

entries.title: Our own windows can be moved, resized and zoomed; and the host had never received real input until now
entries.lede: Client-decorated windows (mailo on Blitz, the future apps) gain interactive move and resize with the pointer's press serial, maximise, minimise and fullscreen, the window's state readable by the frame, and an invisible 7 px resize margin around the visible frame with the right cursors, excluded from the window geometry and the blur. On the way the agent found that the host had never created a pointer or keyboard at all: the toolkit routes a seat that already exists at bind time through a different callback than a seat announced later, and the handler ignored it. Every acceptance so far drove surfaces through the debug-injection path, which bypasses Wayland input, so nothing noticed. Fixed in the same branch; everything believed about live typing, hovering and clicking through the host is unverified until re-run with a real mouse and keyboard.
notes: Headless KWin with fake input: a titlebar drag moves the frame by the drag; a bottom-right margin drag grows 480x320 to 580x380 with the origin fixed; maximise fills the output minus the bar; cursor shapes default, nwse-resize, ns-resize; 5 s idle at 0 frames. Nested cosmic-comp: maximise and fullscreen work; a move with the pointer elsewhere is refused, nothing sent.

For the compositor fork list: cosmic-comp 1.8 configures every floating window as tiled on all four edges, so no resize margin can exist there; and neither cosmic-comp nor KWin lets a client tile itself left, right or centred (no placement request in xdg_toplevel, none in cosmic's toplevel manager, KDE's set_position is KDE-only), so the window menu ships Fill only.
The document's own CSS cursor is now applied; it used to be recorded and never shown.

entries.title: A macOS-grade level control for volume and brightness, in three looks for the pick
entries.lede: The user said a plain slider is too simple. The new level control has a thick capsule track with the glyph inside it, knocked out two-tone where the fill covers it; the glyph follows the level (speaker waves 0 to 3, a mute slash, sun rays that grow); while dragging the fill follows the pointer with no easing, set from outside it eases over the quick token; a press swells the track with the spring; dragging past an end stretches the capsule a few pixels and it springs back; keys step a sixteenth. Three looks: Capsule (glyph inside), CapsuleKnob (the older look with a separate handle) and Segments (sixteen staggered squares). The same wave built the OSD card: top right under the bar, a title line and the control in control-center module metrics, dropping in from above and fading out with the host unmapping at settle.
notes: Recommendation: Capsule. It is the current macOS form and carries glyph, level and mute in one shape; Segments look dated and the knob adds a handle that means nothing on a read-only OSD.

Measured: a set from outside follows the ease-out curve (131 vs 130 px at a quarter of the time); a drag is under the pointer 16 ms after the move; the swell is 27 to 29 px; the stretch is 3 px and springs back; Reduced motion has no stretch.

Blitz finding: one document holding about 60 tinted cards loses layers (every card vanished), so the sheet renders each row on its own. Blitz has no pointer capture, so dragging out of the control's hit zone lets go.

entries.title: A rich-text editing surface for the mail composer, with no fork of the renderer
entries.lede: mailo keeps its own editor core and document model and draws its own caret and selection; quire now gives it the surface underneath. The spike found that the renderer's window-event hook runs before Blitz consumes an event, so IME preedit and commit reach the surface without patching anything, and everything needed for hit-testing and caret geometry was already public. The surface delivers typing, composition steps, paste with HTML, cut and copy, and pointer presses resolved to a text position (element plus byte offset), reports caret and selection rectangles, and sets the IME cursor area. A Harness driver types a Zhuyin composition in tests; an example window prints every input for a manual IME check.
notes: Two Blitz defaults had to be blocked: a press starts its own painted text selection, and a click on a non-field element clears the focus.

Limits recorded: no automated test drives the real window's IME (re-check at every toolchain bump); no pointer capture during a drag; Tab still moves focus; CJK lines do not wrap at word boundaries; a caret exactly at an inline object's boundary resolves to after it.

657 tests; quire v0.1.5, v0.1.6 and v0.1.7 went to mailo in one day: nine wave-two, seven wave-three and nine wave-four component gaps, the Phase B host (contexts, sealed frames, HTML parser, clipboard, focus, frame links), and this surface.

entries.title: Five app icons ship in three styles, one family across procedural and model-derived faces
entries.lede: The user took the recommendation: mail in monochrome slate and photos in monochrome rose from the FLUX.2 Klein faces, files in solid ochre, terminal in monochrome jade and notes on paper with a clay spot, all procedural, at the muted chroma. A ship manifest exports every app at the freedesktop sizes, their doubles and the 1.5x sizes, drawn directly per size, into assets under the repository licence. Three styles ship: Colour, Muted at a lower chroma, and Monochrome exported neutral and tinted at run time by the Space, the accent or nothing, through a pure re-tint over RGBA bytes in the design crate that the shell also applies to third-party icons. A consistency test measures silhouette, bevel, shade and shadow across the five.
notes: Sizes 16, 22, 24, 32, 36, 44, 48, 64, 72, 96, 128, 256, 512; 195 files, 6.1 MB. The 1024 master is not exported (design/08 stops the double at 256; the grain would make it 1.2 MB each).
The Paper plate is the one consistency exception: too close to white to show the top arc, so its bevel reads through the bottom shade and rim only.
Shell side: pick the file by style and size x scale, re-tint third-party icons after plating and before caching, never symbolic icons, and key the cache by icon, size, scale, style and tint.

entries.date: 2026-09-25 · Milestone 0 on the live KDE session
entries.title: The host passes its Milestone 0 acceptance on the real KWin session at scale 2
entries.lede: With the KDE session unlocked, the same acceptance the host passed on nested cosmic-comp ran on the user's live Plasma 6 desktop: one 4K output at scale 2, NVIDIA over Vulkan, compositor blur on. The bar reserves its 32 px and paints its probe colour; blur behind the bar drops the variance by 99.98 % while the checkerboard below it stays sharp; the dock's hover sweep renders a frame per callback in every present mode with sub-millisecond frames and idles at zero frames, zero commits and zero main-thread wakeups; two surfaces share one device. The fractional-scale item was written for a 1.5 output and the display is at 2 now, so only its buffer and checker checks apply, and those pass.
notes: The first attempt failed before any demo ran: the invoking shell had no runtime-directory variable, so nothing could find the compositor socket.

Fractional item: buffer 3840x64 for 1920x32 logical, checker runs of exactly 4 device pixels, preferred scale 240; its screen-row check failed because the capture held no bar at all (spectacle shot before the surface was mapped or after the demo exited), so it is a capture-timing question, not a rendering one. Recorded as shell-host F45.

entries.date: 2026-09-25 · sill Milestone 2 wallpaper, and pixel snapping wired through
entries.title: The shell draws its own wallpaper, after two bugs in two repos; every surface reads its scale and snaps to device pixels
entries.lede: The wallpaper service reads COSMIC's background record, resizes with Lanczos into a per-output cache and cross-fades on light and dark; the surface is a background layer that takes no input. It was built and gated a day before it painted anything. The first cause was in the host: after every present it dropped the redraw request that the image loader raised from another thread mid-render, so a decoded image never got a second paint (found with a standalone host demo, fixed by keeping host-thread and loader-thread requests apart). The second was in the shell: Taffy placed the fixed-position root against a zero-height parent, so the page was zero pixels tall. With both fixed the wallpaper is on by default and its acceptance passes 4 of 4. The same push wires quire's pixel snapping into every surface: each root reads the surface's live fractional scale and the host runs the snapping pass before each paint.
notes: Idle with the full wiring at 1x, 20 s: bar 4→4 frames, dock 3→3, wallpaper 3→3, launcher 0. A first reading of 13 idle frames was the counters crossing the clock's minute repaint.

Host demo before the fix: a CSS background and a 512 px img stayed on the fallback colour; after: file, data-URL and CSS sources all show the image within about 5 ms of the swap, then 5 s idle at zero frames. Callbacks were never withheld by cosmic-comp, so the suspected #2777 path was not the cause.
Still to do: a hairline screenshot on the nested output at scale 1.5 to see the snapping on screen.

entries.title: Round five: eight muted colourways per app, and how far the colour can be pushed
entries.lede: The user asked for more colours. The palette grew to eight hues 45 degrees apart (clay, ochre, sage, jade, teal, slate, plum, rose), still capped at the round-four chroma, and each app is shown in its recommended dialect across all eight. A second sheet shows three hues at three chroma levels so the saturation ceiling can be judged; a third is the swatch board with every colour's OKLCh values printed, so a pick can be named. No model ran: the mail and photos rows are the round-three Klein picks re-tinted.
notes: Legibility: every hue at every level scores 3.0 to 4.1 against the dock pill on both Space frames in light and dark; the plate's mid lightness does that work, so hue never decides it.

Space frames: on Work (hue 268) slate and its neighbours teal and plum sit well, ochre and clay clash mildly; on Home (152) sage and jade sit well, plum and rose clash. At the lowest chroma the clash is faint because the frames are nearly grey; at the highest they vibrate.
Bolder levels: at chroma 0.15 ochre, jade and teal leave sRGB and the candy look returns; 0.11 keeps every hue in gamut and is the step to take if the set should be louder.
Recommendation, one hue per app: mail slate, files ochre, terminal jade (monochrome), notes a clay spot, photos rose. Five apps, five parts of the wheel.

entries.title: Round four: one muted palette, no gradients, four dialects to mix across the set
entries.lede: The direction after round three: fewer gradients, less vibrant colour, and not every icon from the same recipe. Every icon keeps one skeleton (the squircle, the same light, a thin top bevel arc, bottom shade, drop shadow, emboss depth and grain) and one OKLCh palette capped at chroma 0.07 with six named hues (slate, teal, sage, ochre, clay, plum); plates are one colour with at most a faint tonal shift. Four dialects: Monochrome tone-on-tone (plate and symbol share a hue and differ in lightness), Graphite (near-black plate, light symbol), Paper (quire's paper plate, ink symbol, one spot of colour at most), and Solid (one flat muted colour, white symbol). Mail, files and photos also get their round-three Klein pick re-tinted into Monochrome, keeping Klein's emboss. A second sheet shows the whole set in Monochrome tinted by a Space, and two settings keys (icons.style: Colour, Muted, Monochrome; icons.monochrome_tint: Space, Accent, Neutral) are registered for it. No model ran this round.
notes: Recommendation (three dialects across five apps): mail = Monochrome slate, Klein variant; files = Solid ochre, procedural (the Klein files is blotchy); terminal = Graphite; notes = Paper with the ochre spot on the fold; photos = Monochrome clay, Klein variant.
Weak spots: Monochrome and Solid are the least distinct pair; a Paper plate nearly disappears at 16 px on the light ground, so the ink symbol has to carry it.
cargo deny's advisory check fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0192 (ttf-parser unmaintained) through the Blitz stack, on master too; licences pass. Recorded, not silenced.

entries.title: Round three pressed the symbol into a two-hue bevelled plate; the user picked procedural for terminal and notes, Klein's face for mail, files and photos
entries.lede: After round two the user gave a reference direction: symbols embossed into the plate with no outlines or strokes, a matte finish, the plate's bevel catching light in a few crisp narrow spots, a soft two-hue gradient ground per app, no frosted glass, no text. The procedural renderer now draws filled layers raised, recessed or flush with an inner light edge and a soft shade, mixes each app's two-hue ground in OKLCh, and finishes the plate with a narrow top highlight arc, a bottom shade and one specular point; the emboss drops out at 16 and 32 px so the small sizes stay flat. FLUX.2 Klein rendered the same brief two ways: the embossed symbol on a surface that becomes the plate face, and the whole tile re-masked with our squircle. Qwen ran mail and terminal only. The pick is the user's; the agent's reading is that the procedural set is best at every size, Klein's face mode has the most convincing clay emboss but blurs at 16 and washes files and notes to pastel, and a hybrid (Klein's face as the material study on the procedural plate) is open.
notes: design/08 §2.9 records the embossed rules for app icons only; small symbolic glyphs keep Lucide's one stroke. docs/icons-bakeoff.md 'Round three' has the full comparison.
New tools: `tools/icons face` plates a model-drawn surface or tile, `tools/icons strips` makes the 512/48/32/16 pick sheets, tools/icons/round3.sh runs the set.

entries.title: The bar, dock and launcher take the polish pass on the nested compositor, over a real wallpaper
entries.lede: Every shell surface now writes the shell type scale and the material stack from the settings around its root. The bar's app name and clock sit in menu-bar pills and the workspaces form one segmented group; text menus are 22 px rows with a hairline separator and a rounded highlight. The dock pill is a squircle with quire's dock metrics, every tile on a paper plate, running dots on the baseline through a bounce. The launcher's card is a squircle sized to its content, its measured rect drives the panel's input and blur and the catcher's hole, and the surface grew room for the card's shadow. Fourteen new settings keys, three moved defaults, and a generated test wallpaper behind every acceptance run.
notes: Acceptance: dock 6/6 (window maximises to 1260 of 1360; hover sweep 39 frames for 38 callbacks; idle 0 frames in 5 s; squircle corner probe tells inside from outside), bar 8/8 (idle 0 commits), launcher 6/6 in release: warm open min 64, p50 68, max 100 ms; first open 153 ms. The same build failed the 100 ms gate at load average 18 and passed at 8.

Gaps recorded as Q66 to Q70: design/22 rows (added in quire v0.1.3), material keys read from `extra` until ds-settings had fields (v0.1.3 has them; the switch is in progress), pill radius 22 vs the brief's 18 (same curve at 60 px, shadow radius differs), popup side room 24 px cuts a 28 px menu shadow, MagnifyParams design defaults.

entries.date: 2026-09-25 · quire polish pass and icon bake-off
entries.title: The design system gains the layers macOS stacks; icon round two is abstract, and the procedural set speaks the language
entries.lede: After comparing the shell with macOS, the design system gained a material stack (a vibrancy boost baked into the tint, a 1 px inner highlight, a hairline, a contact shadow and an ambient one), continuous-curvature squircle corners, a shell type scale (13 px bar items, 22 px menu rows, a 22 px launcher field), menu-bar hover pills, dock metrics with running dots and placeholder plates, and a launcher card that fits its content. The gallery's Polish page prints each rendering beside the macOS number it targets. The icon bake-off ran on both local models and produced clean, readable icons, but they are photoreal objects on plates; the verdict was 'too realistic', so round two goes abstract in the paper-and-ink language, with a procedural alternative built from the tokens. Round two ran: both models with a flat paper-cut-out brief, and a procedural set drawn from the tokens (one stroke weight, Post corners, the frame grain, four colours on the plate). The procedural set is coherent by construction and reads at every size; the generated sets moved away from clay renders but keep a second line weight (Klein) or bevels and drop shadows (Qwen). The pick is the user's.
notes: Polish values are all configurable (design/22 keys per item); the docs mark each as settled with its macOS reference and confidence.
Bake-off numbers: FLUX.2 Klein 4B renders in 3 to 4 s warm at 12 GB; Qwen-Image-2512 in 70 to 90 s at 14.7 GB (cannot share the GPU). Qwen gave the cleaner raw set; both failed the terminal subject.

Round two: Klein 3.0 s per render at 11.1 GB peak, Qwen 67 to 78 s at 15.0 GB. Procedural: a 20 to 40 line spec per icon, seconds to render, every export size drawn rather than downscaled. Full comparison in docs/icons-bakeoff.md 'Round two'.

entries.title: The launcher opens in about 60 ms with apps, windows, settings and a calculator, on the same menu as everything else
entries.lede: The first delivery gate of the program. Two warm surfaces (a transparent catcher and the panel) are toggled through one shared link, so opening never spawns anything. The search core runs every provider on its own thread, stamps results by generation and drops stale ones; queries reach their first results in microseconds. Providers: applications (with desktop actions), open windows, system commands gated on what logind allows, a calculator on fend, and settings keys from the installed schemas plus COSMIC's own pages. The panel is the design system's command palette, keyboard-first, with Ctrl+K opening a row's actions as the same menu the bar and dock use.
notes: Acceptance on nested cosmic-comp (release build): warm open 52 to 80 ms, p50 57 (the budget is 100); first open 106 ms; both surfaces exist hidden from startup; a second toggle hides, a catcher click closes; 5 s idle after hide adds 0 frames on both surfaces.

Both crashes are fixed at the source (motion tasks are owned by their scope; focus goes through a host seam) and the launcher's workarounds are gone: the palette fills its panel with no dim box, rows show the app's own icon, the selection follows the pointer, and the actions menu hangs from the selected row. A 20-toggle stress at 150 ms spacing leaves the daemon healthy.

Not yet: IME verified live (needs your unlocked session and fcitx5: dev/ime-probe.sh prints the commands), the launcher on the output under the pointer, and system commands (logged, not run, until a session control exists).
Latency re-measurement pending a quiet machine: with a 28-core job running, warm opens read about 117 ms p50 versus 57 ms earlier.

entries.title: The dock launches, magnifies, badges and quits real apps on cosmic-comp
entries.lede: The second shell surface, on the same design system as the bar. Behind it the application index (353 desktop entries on this machine, icons resolved through the theme chain), launching through transient systemd scopes or D-Bus activation with an activation token, a pins file, and LauncherEntry badges from the session bus. The dock reserves its height, magnifies tiles at the compositor's own frame rate while the pointer is over it and goes back to zero frames when it leaves, launches a pinned app on click, shows a badge within a frame of the signal, and opens the design system's context menu on a right click.
notes: Acceptance on nested cosmic-comp: reserve 72 px; a one-second hover sweep renders 52 frames for 52 callbacks then 0 frames over 5 s idle; COSMIC Terminal launched in its own scope with its running dot 0.5 s later; a count badge turned red 131 ms after the emitter sent it; a right-click opened the menu with the window, Remove from Dock and Quit.

After the adoption pass the pill is the Dock material's own Space-gradient tint with its radius and shadow, and the hover label stays hidden while a menu is open. Still open in the design system: a radius override for the pill setting, icon sizes above 22 px, and a caller-driven tooltip.
Not yet built: Open at Login, drag ghost, file drops, minimize targets, sounds; auto-hide is wired but not exercised.

entries.title: The bar runs as a real shell surface on cosmic-comp: workspaces, status items, menus, zero idle frames
entries.lede: The first shell surface built on the design system. The sill daemon starts, takes its single-instance lock, spawns the services (UPower, NetworkManager, PipeWire, the status-notifier tray, the COSMIC toplevel and workspace protocols on their own connection) and puts one bar per output on the nested compositor. The bar reserves its 32 px, sits idle at zero frames, and its clock and status menus are the design system's Menu opened as real popups. Every stylesheet and render passes the coherence lint, so it is the same menu mailo will get.
notes: Updated after the design-system adoption pass: the bar is the Space gradient with grain, status items sit on the frame inks, the tray shows each app's own icon (coloured ones as images, the rest recoloured to the ink), and the popup is transparent around its card. The launcher panel in the first shot is the M4 work in progress on the same compositor.
Acceptance on nested cosmic-comp and on KWin: exclusive zone 32 px; five seconds idle adds 0 frames and 0 commits; the clock menu opens and dismisses; the popup is transparent around its card.

What the live bar shows here: the focused app, workspace pills (drag to reorder), tray icons (stand-in glyphs until the design system can draw an app's own icon, which is being added), volume, Wi-Fi, the clock in the local zone.
Below the daemon's bar in the second shot is the demo bar with fake services and its clock menu open.

entries.title: The host passes four of the five acceptance items on the real compositor; compositor blur makes the bar vanish
entries.lede: Nested cosmic-comp 1.8.0 turns out to run with the screen off once GL vblank sync is disabled, so the deferred run happened today. The bar reserves its 32 px, fractional scale maps pixel for pixel, two surfaces share one device, and the dock hover sweep renders every frame with zero idle frames. Blur is the exception: with a blur region requested, cosmic-comp stops drawing the bar at all (one run captured a blank frame), while the same client passes on KWin. The acceptance check now also requires the checkerboard to stay visible so a blank frame can never read as a perfect blur. An investigation is running.
notes: Dock sweep on cosmic: 2059 frames for 2059 callbacks, 0.27 ms median, 0.39 ms p95; five seconds idle: 0 frames, 0 commits, 0 main-thread wakeups.
Two surfaces on one device: the second costs 1.4 MB.

Blur: the bar is composited with blur off and disappears with blur on; the cause (our buffer/region or a cosmic-comp bug on the nested GL path) is being isolated with a plain shm client and the AMD adapter.

entries.title: The design system exists: every component on review pages, in both themes and six accents
entries.lede: Forty-one components, the token tables, eight materials, forty-six animations and the Space editor are built and green (about 310 tests), and the gallery renders them through the real Blitz pipeline. Its first run caught thirteen defects (text inputs at replaced-element size, an empty toast pill on every root, invisible undo labels, a class collision between the text field and the Space editor's colour field); all are fixed, then a polish pass scoped the reset with :where, moved every spacing in every sheet onto the spacing tokens, and made the colour field's dots round. These are the sheets after both passes. The migration brief has gone to the mailo session.
notes: Two root causes behind most of the list: one shared class name between two components, and a reset rule that outranked every single-class component rule.

Open: a Blitz hit-testing bug (a lone inline-flex button beside only inline content receives no click; reproduction test written for an upstream report) and overlay bounds that follow the content height.

entries.title: The real host passes the Milestone 0 acceptance: one process, many surfaces, no idle frames
entries.lede: The spike is retired. The production host (calloop loop, one GPU device, shared renderer, layer surfaces, popups, input, IME, clipboard, blur, fractional scale) runs the same five acceptance items on its demos in a nested KWin and passes them all; 162 tests; the same numbers as the spike within noise.
notes: Dock hover sweep: 73 frames for 73 callbacks, 0.89 ms median; five seconds idle: zero frames, zero commits, zero main-thread wakeups.
Two driver facts recorded: wgpu ties an instance to one Wayland display; NVIDIA 615.71 crashes on a surface query after a probe instance is dropped, so probe instances are kept alive.

entries.title: Blitz renders into a layer-shell bar with compositor blur, and the dock hover animates with zero idle frames
entries.lede: The go/no-go item for the whole program passed with no fallback. A Dioxus document draws into a top-anchored layer surface through one shared GPU renderer; the bar reserves its 32 px, the compositor blurs what is behind it, a hover sweep across twelve dock icons renders every frame in about a millisecond, and five seconds of idle produce no frames at all. Two surfaces in one process cost 2 MB more than one. Run in a nested virtual KWin because the session was locked.

Blur: pixel variance inside the bar dropped from 3306 to 0.56.
Fractional scale 1.5 and 1.7 map buffer to screen pixel for pixel; a 2-logical-px checker measures 3 px at 1.5.
NVIDIA on Vulkan works; the AMD iGPU and the GL backend do not present on this machine.

entries.title: A custom-painted widget draws into its own GPU texture inside a Blitz document
entries.lede: The path the terminal, video player and PDF viewer will use: a Rust widget owns a wgpu texture, renders into it each frame, and Blitz composites it as an image. Redraw requests stop after the widget says it is idle. The headless render-to-PNG path and its snapshot test (the CI gate for every surface) also work.
notes: Rendered on the RTX 5070 Ti through Vulkan, offscreen; the CPU path leaves the widget transparent by design.
Snapshot tolerance: at most 2 per channel and 0.1 % of pixels; a deliberate colour change was rejected at 8.2 %.

entries.title: Blur, fractional scale and popups work against KWin from a bare client
entries.lede: Hand-written Wayland protocol handlers (the ones smithay-client-toolkit 0.20 lacks): the compositor advertises blur and honours a region; fractional scale reports this display's real 1.7; an xdg_popup child of a layer surface positions itself with the compositor's own constraint adjustment, and a nested submenu positions relative to it.
notes: Popup 1 configured at (0,28) 180x110 after KWin slid it on-screen; popup 2 at (164,13) 160x90.
24 tests: rounded-strip regions against a raster oracle, positioner tables, scale rounding.
No screenshot: the capture tool returned transparent images from that run; fixed for the next spike.

entries.title: cosmic-comp runs nested inside the KDE session with every protocol we need
entries.lede: One script starts a nested COSMIC compositor as a window, records its socket, and lists its globals. It advertises layer-shell v5, background blur, fractional scale, viewporter, COSMIC toplevel and workspace protocols, and text-input v3. ghostty runs inside it; stopping it leaves the host untouched.
notes: Works on the NVIDIA path directly; the AMD fallback was not needed.
Frosted glass is set through com.system76.CosmicTheme.{Dark,Light}/v2/frosted; 1.8.0 reads only v2.

entries.title: Sixteen Blitz CSS probes settle what the design system may use
entries.lede: Each probe renders a tiny document headlessly and checks pixels. Transitions, keyframes, custom properties, animation restart, SVG currentColor, fonts, color-mix and timers all work. Attribute selectors only match with a namespace prefix, focus-visible is always false, ellipsis clips instead of fading, and no backend does backdrop-filter. The design system's CSS emitter and lint now encode these.
notes: Fallbacks adopted: [*|data-x] selectors, a data-modality attribute for focus rings, mask-image fades for truncation, compositor blur only.
